<description>
**Problem:** When the automatic onion service has no dedicated `-bind=<addr>=onion`, Tor forwards incoming connections to the first normal P2P bind. A wildcard onion bind also fails to identify incoming Tor connections. In either case, network classification is incorrect and Tor peers may inherit permissions granted to the Tor daemon's IP address.

**Fix:** Refuse startup when `-listenonion` is enabled and an explicit `-bind` configuration lacks a dedicated, non-wildcard onion bind or includes a wildcard onion bind, following [the recommendation in #34892](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34892#issuecomment-5541662236). Users should add a specific `-bind=<addr>=onion` or set `-listenonion=0`.

Because `-listenonion` is enabled by default when listening, existing configurations with only a normal `-bind` must also be updated. Nodes without explicit `-bind` options retain the default dedicated onion listener.
</description>

[2026-10-06] c:6018333697 comment by schildbach (contributor):
Keep in mind that when running in a container, it is considered best practise to bind to `0.0.0.0` / `[::]` rather than a specific IP. That is because most container engines (e.g. Docker) use dynamic IPs.

The issue that `0.0.0.0` / `[::]` are unsuitable to pass via Tor control should imho be solved by a second configuration option, as suggested in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/25094.
</new_statements>
